title: Lawsuit Details Alleged Sexual Assault at Fraternity Party Near University of Chicago
snippet: A 19-year-old woman has filed a lawsuit against Alpha Delta Phi, alleging she was incapacitated and sexually assaulted at an off-campus fraternity house near the University of Chicago.
content:
A 19-year-old woman has filed a lawsuit in Cook County Circuit Court alleging she was sexually assaulted at an off-campus fraternity house near the University of Chicago, shedding light once again on allegations of misconduct within campus-adjacent Greek life.

The complaint, filed Monday by an individual identified as Jane Doe, names Alpha Delta Phi Inc. and the Chicago Society of Alpha Delta Phi as defendants. The lawsuit details an incident from Feb. 7, when Doe—who is not a student at the university—attended an open party at the fraternity house with friends after seeing an event invitation on social media.

Allegations of Spiked Drinks and Assault

According to court documents, Doe consumed two drinks over two hours before accepting a shot from a fraternity member. Shortly after taking the drink, she experienced severe physical distress, lightheadedness, and impaired vision—symptoms she believes were caused by a laced beverage.

The lawsuit alleges the fraternity member directed her to a secluded upstairs bedroom, ignoring her visible physical impairment. Doe states that she rapidly lost the ability to physically or verbally resist his advances. Although she managed to ask him to use protection, he refused and assaulted her before leaving her unconscious on the bed.

When Doe's friends tried to search for her upstairs, other fraternity members initially blocked their path, the lawsuit claims. A friend eventually located her unconscious, helped her leave the house, and brought her to a nearby residence hall. The following morning, Doe discovered bloodstains on her clothing and sought medical evaluation at Illinois Masonic Hospital, where clinicians completed a sexual assault evidence collection kit.

Fraternity Suspends Member as Investigations Continue

Doe subsequently filed reports with the Chicago Police Department and spoke briefly with University of Chicago campus police. The civil suit seeks a jury trial and damages exceeding $200,000, alongside efforts to force policy changes within Greek organizations operating near campus.

In a statement, the national leadership of Alpha Delta Phi stated it suspended the member involved upon learning of the allegations, calling the conduct described "deeply troubling and inconsistent with our values." The local Chicago chapter referred inquiries to the national body.

The University of Chicago noted that fraternities are not recognized as official student organizations by the institution, but confirmed it is prepared to assist Chicago police with their investigation. The university community has recently been unsettled by multiple reports of misconduct, including a separate, unlinked sexual assault reported earlier this month at another off-campus fraternity house. Chicago police confirmed investigations into both incidents remain open.
